newsitem.title: UK: Britain's SFA fines Kleinwort Benson.
newsitem.headline: Britain's SFA fines Kleinwort Benson.

text.p: British financial watchdog the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) on Thursday reprimanded Kleinwort Benson Securities for "internal control and other failings" and fined it 30,000 pounds ($50,660).

The SFA said in a statement it had also disciplined two former Kleinwort Benson employees for mismarking positions. It said both Alistair Truelove and Philip Steel had agreed to a settlement of proceedings against them. Kleinwort Benson admitted failings and will pay the SFA 7,900 pounds in costs.

Truelove, who was a trader in European convertible notes and warrants at Kleinwort Benson, has been reprimanded, fined 7,500 pounds and will pay 3,000 pounds towards costs while Steel, his assistant, has been reprimanded and will pay 2,000 pounds towards costs, the SFA said.

The watchdog said that between the beginning of July 1995 and the beginning of September 1995, Truelove and Steel "adopted a practice of marking positions on the European convertibles and warrants book which was neither in accordance with SFA's rules nor with its (Kleinwort Benson's) own mark to market policy".

Marking to market is the process by which a firm calculates the value of a trading position based on the daily closing price, thereby reflecting the unrealised profit and loss on an outstanding position. Discrepancies were detected at the beginning of September 1995 as part of Kleinwort Benson's weekly independent price verification checks, the SFA said.

But at no time from July to September did the strategy employed by Truelove and Steel "or the consequent falsification of valuations of positions in the books and records" of Kleinwort Benson attract the attention of its management. When these were detected, Truelove and Steel were dismissed. ($1=.5922 Pound)
